lines.text: At dawn the ram came. It hit the gate nine times. On the tenth, the gate came down.
Penhallow rode through the gap on his white horse, with his ring blazing and his sword wrapped in fire, and a hundred men behind him.
Bram was standing in the gateway. One old man, with one arm and one old sword. And three half-grown wolfhounds beside him, hackles up.
Stand aside, old man. You're a two. Everyone knows it.
Everyone's wrong about a great many things, my lord.
Then Bram let go of the breath he had been holding since the day the Measurers came. Five rings rose around him. Every one of them his own.
Penhallow's smile slipped. He had five rings too. His were bought.
They met in the gateway. Fire against iron. Penhallow was faster, and younger, and he had two arms. Bram had fifty years.
Rook went for Penhallow's horse. Birk and Tarn went for everyone else. Behind them, the whole village came down off the walls to hold the gap.
But there were too many. Bram was bleeding from three places, and his sword arm was slowing. Penhallow's fire never tired. Borrowed fire doesn't.
Kneel, steward. Kneel, and I'll let the dogs live.
I've knelt to one lord in my life. You're not him.
That was when the flank of Penhallow's army began to scream.
Something huge and black came out of the trees on the south road, and went through three ranks of crimson like a scythe through barley.
He was thinner. He was scarred from nose to tail. And down the back of his neck, starting between his ears, ran a streak of white that had never been there before.
Ash had come home.
Nobody knows how he got out of those tunnels, or how he crossed half a kingdom alone. I think he just went home. Someone had told him to keep me warm, and home was where I'd come.
You're late.
Ash licked the blood off his face. Bram allowed it. He told everyone afterwards that he hadn't.
Rook, Birk and Tarn went mad with joy, and then went mad at Penhallow's men. The flank broke. The gap held.
And on the mountainside, two miles north, I felt a thread I had stopped letting myself feel. It came back like a door kicked open. Thick, and warm, and furious.
I didn't know what had happened. I only knew that Ash was alive, and fighting, and I was still too far away.
So I pulled off my gloves, and ran.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and nineteen, coming soon.
